producer_report.summary: Added the core of the rebase before landing to crates/athena-core/src/gh/landing.rs. `plan_rebase(git, onto, head, landed, sign)` is a pure, stack-aware plan. It replays the first-parent commits from the fork with main up to the branch head, oldest first, onto origin's main. It returns `Rebase::Current`, `Moved{onto, landed, tip, records_only}` or `Conflict{commit, text}`. A conflict in the job's own landing commit is a hold. A conflict in an earlier commit is kept as records only: `commit_with_records` builds a records-only image of that commit and merges it onto the running tip, so its records/ paths stay and its code is dropped. The carried commit's message drops the Athena-* trailers and gets an `Athena-Records-Only: <old commit>` line. `plan_rebase` checks that marker on `landed` first and returns Conflict, so a job whose only commit is a records-only carry is held, not read as Current. `rebase_job_branch(git, state, remote_name, default_branch, job, verified_fp, ui)` returns `Unchecked` for a published head that is not the early head, a failed or empty fetch, or no landing commit. Otherwise it takes the repository lock, runs the plan and moves the branch with `reset_keep` on Moved. It never pushes. `Rebase`, `plan_rebase` and `rebase_job_branch` are re-exported from gh/mod.rs. CHANGELOG.md and docs/design/async-drain.md section 6 carry notes. They cover the records-only carry, clean earlier commits still riding along, the re-check rule not covering stacked content, queue order being pass order, a Moved result possibly changing verified content (build job 7), and the drain wiring as a follow-up. drain.rs is untouched. I added 11 tests in `rebase_tests`, run against real git repositories and a real bare origin.

open_issues: Deviation 1 from the plan: `rebase_job_branch` has no `sign` argument, so it takes 7 parameters (git, state, remote_name, default_branch, job, verified_fingerprint, ui). It reads `git.signs_commits()?` itself, as `resync_onto_merge` does. With 8 parameters clippy's too_many_arguments fires, and the plan said to add no `#[allow]`. `plan_rebase` still takes `sign`.

Deviation 2: the plan's plan_rebase_parentless_commit_is_an_error test became plan_rebase_unrelated_history_is_an_error. A range commit with no parent cannot occur once merge-base succeeds, so the test checks that unrelated histories make `git merge-base` fail and surface as an Err. The in-code parentless bail has no test.
I added one unplanned rule: `plan_rebase` also returns Current when `landed` is already an ancestor of `onto`, meaning it is already on main. The stack above it is not moved in that case.

This is the plan's open question, and the drain follow-up must settle it.

learnings: Git::replay and `git log --format=%B` give a message with an extra trailing blank line. Re-committing it with `commit_tree -F -` keeps the extra newline, so the replayed message is not byte-equal to the original. `plan_rebase` trims it to one newline. Git::replay itself still adds the extra newline.

`Git::commit_with_records(base, records_from, ..)` replaces all of records/ in `base` with that of `records_from`. Called with the commit's parent as `base` it gives a records-only image of the commit. Merging it with `merge_tree(parent, tip, image)` carries only that commit's own records changes.

`landed_commit_from_records` takes the oldest commit that added outcome.json for the job and checks that verification.json holds the fingerprint. It reads no trailers, so a records-only carry would be found as the landing commit. The `Athena-Records-Only:` marker check in `plan_rebase` handles that.

`fetch_remote_branch` brings the tip object into the work repository without writing a ref. A commit pushed to origin by another clone is therefore not in the work repository until `rebase_job_branch` fetches it.
Bash in this role blocks `tail`, pipes and reads outside the working directory. Saved tool-result files are not readable with Grep.
